question_text: What is the use of dry ice?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What dry ice is
lines: Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide, CO₂ in
It is obtained by compressing carbon
dioxide gas to a liquid and then
letting it expand rapidly, which cools
At ordinary pressure it does not melt
into a liquid. It changes straight from
the solid to the gas, and that is why it
steps.why: The name is worth explaining because it is the reason the substance is useful. Ordinary ice melts and wets whatever it is packed with; solid carbon dioxide goes straight to gas at ordinary pressure, so nothing is left behind.
common_mistakes: Writing that dry ice is solid water or frozen ice without water. Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide.
Writing that dry ice melts to a liquid. At ordinary pressure it changes directly from solid to gas.
steps.memory_tip: Dry because it leaves no liquid behind: solid carbon dioxide goes straight to gas.
steps.margin_note: Naming the substance as solid CO₂ is the first thing to write, before any use.

steps.label: Its use

lines.text: Dry ice is used as a refrigerant

lines: It is used to keep ice cream and frozen
food cold during storage and transport.
Because it turns straight into gas, it
does not wet the food it is packed with.
steps.why: A refrigerant is a substance used to keep other things cold. Dry ice is much colder than ordinary ice and leaves no liquid behind, so it is used where food has to stay frozen and dry at the same time.
common_mistakes: Writing that dry ice is used as a fuel. It is not burnt; it is used for cooling.
Giving the use with no mention of what dry ice is. One opening line naming it as solid CO₂ completes the answer.
steps.memory_tip: Refrigerant for ice cream and frozen food — cooling is the use this question is asking for.
steps.margin_note: Naming ice cream and frozen food makes the use concrete rather than general.

insider_note: Naming the substance and naming the use are the two halves of this answer: dry ice is solid carbon dioxide, and it is used as a refrigerant for ice cream and frozen food. Saying that it leaves nothing wet behind shows why that use follows.
